content: 1. Perform annual screenings for symptoms of depression in all patients diagnosed with diabetes. For individuals with a prior history of depression, conduct these assessments more frequently. 2. Utilize validated screening tools that are appropriate for the patient’s age, and understand that individuals who screen positive for depression may require additional, more detailed evaluations. 3. Evaluate for depression when a patient is diagnosed with complications related to diabetes or experiences significant changes in their overall medical condition. 4. Refer patients exhibiting depressive symptoms to behavioral health professionals or healthcare providers who are trained in evidence-based treatments for depression. This referral should be integrated into a collaborative care approach alongside the diabetes management team.
